criteria.criterion: Both shard-test-executing subprocesses in execute_shard() — baseline pytest and mutmut run — are wrapped in OS-enforced sandbox denying writes outside allow-list; venv excluded.
The enforcement test trips the deny under mutmut run specifically.
The sandbox demonstrably DENIES: probe writing outside allow-list exits non-zero and file absent; same probe inside allow-list succeeds. Observes enforcement, not construction.
macOS uses Seatbelt sandbox-exec with generated (allow default) + (deny file-write*) + allow-list profile, three probes verified.
Linux uses bwrap, probed at runtime, fails closed without it. No unshare fallback.

citation.description: Ticket comment attests: 'Linux enforcement was measured by hand in a ubuntu:24.04 container (write outside DENIED, write inside succeeded, rm -rf <protected>/* DENIED with target surviving)'. The @live enforcement tests exist in test_mutation_sandbox.py and would run on Linux with bwrap available.

criteria.criterion: The Linux write-deny is proven on Linux, not inferred from macOS: three probes measured by hand in ubuntu:24.04 container.
The sandbox wrapper preserves the existing mutmut run --max-children 1 concurrency contract.
With no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED.
REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED=1 waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING; a silent unsandboxed fallback is rejected.
Enforcement is an OS facility invoked in-process, never a CI-provider feature, works from developer laptop.
HOME is set to non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses; verified by running a child and asserting HOME it observes, plus binding test.
probe() verifies BOTH mechanisms FUNCTIONALLY, never by shutil.which. Verified by test_bwrap_present_but_unable_to_namespace_is_not_offered and test_seatbelt_present_but_not_enforcing_is_not_offered.
On a CI runner (CI truthy) with no mechanism the gate proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a WARNING; on a workstation it still ABORTS.
Bubblewrap is installed on the Linux CI lanes (_build-and-test.yml, _mutation.yml).
A usable sandbox is used even on CI — CI is a fallback for the ABSENCE of a mechanism, never a licence to skip a working one.

findings.criterion: With no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero with a message naming `REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED`. Verified by a test stubbing the mechanism absent and asserting that literal appears in stderr.
findings.detail: The implementation does NOT abort unconditionally when no sandbox mechanism is available. When the `CI` environment variable is truthy, `wrap()` proceeds UNSANDBOXED with a WARNING instead of raising `SandboxUnavailable` (scripts/mutation_sandbox.py lines 262-271). The criterion as written says 'the run ABORTS non-zero' with no qualification. The test `test_no_mechanism_raises_and_names_the_opt_out` only tests the non-CI path (passes `env={}`). The ticket's own comments explicitly acknowledge this discrepancy: 'AC8 was reworded to fit the code... The criterion says: with no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS non-zero. Full stop. The implementation's CI branch does NOT abort — it waives with a warning.' The criterion text was never updated to reflect the CI exception.
findings.title: AC7/AC8: abort-on-no-mechanism criterion not met — CI branch waives instead of aborting

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
